$comment: Which Kokkos backend you get is decided by the pratico devShell, not by this file: `nix develop nix-config/labs/pratico#ww3` puts a Serial+OpenMP Kokkos on the CMake search path, `#cuda` puts a CUDA/ADA89 one there. These presets only choose build type, instrumentation, and -- for CUDA -- the compiler nvcc insists on. Presets schema 10 needs CMake >= 4.1; the lab shell pins 4.4.2.

configurePresets.name: serial-debug
configurePresets.$comment: Kokkos_ENABLE_DEBUG_BOUNDS_CHECK is deliberately not set here: it is an option of the Kokkos *build*, not of a consumer, so it is fixed by the pinned Kokkos derivation in nix-config/labs/pratico and cannot be switched on from this file. The safety net is AddressSanitizer + UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer plus WW_DETERMINISTIC. The name describes the build type, not the backend: OpenMP is the default execution space in #ww3, so code that must run on Serial names Kokkos::Serial explicitly.

configurePresets.name: openmp-release
configurePresets.$comment: x86-64-v3 is AVX2 + FMA: every machine this lab targets, and no runtime dispatch.

configurePresets.name: cuda-release
configurePresets.displayName: Release on the CUDA backend (needs `just cuda` / the #cuda shell)
configurePresets.$comment: Kokkos rejects a plain g++ once CUDA is on, so the compiler must be nvcc_wrapper (on PATH in #cuda). The pinned CUDA Kokkos is built for one architecture only, ADA89 (RTX 4090); an H100 needs a Kokkos rebuild with HOPPER90, not a change here.
